findings.title: Azure SQL backup storage redundancy is not bound to the signed region pair
evidence: 3-azure-design/evidence/stratton-operations-reliability-contract.json uses automated PITR backups and LTR/failover controls but specifies no SQL backupStorageRedundancy value.

3-azure-design/evidence/stratton-aff4-handoff.json module 9 and requiredParametersWithoutProductionDefaults omit SQL STR/LTR backup storage redundancy, and its compileTimeAndPolicyAssertions contain no guard against GRS or GZRS.
3-azure-design/evidence/stratton-citadel-landing-zone-contract.json states that replication is limited to the approved pair and that no implicit Azure geo-pair is accepted.
Microsoft Learn states that new Azure SQL databases default to geo-redundant backup storage replicated to a paired region, and that LRS or ZRS must be selected to keep STR and LTR backups in-region.
findings.risk: A Phase 4/5 implementation that follows the current handoff can silently accept Azure SQL's default GRS backup setting and replicate highly confidential production backups to an Azure paired region that is not one of the two signed-approved locations. This breaks SR-001, HD-003, VAL-005 and the design's fail-closed sovereignty claim, and can create an unapproved transfer before any runtime control detects it.
boundedRemediation: Add an explicit per-environment Azure SQL STR/LTR backup-storage-redundancy parameter and policy assertion with no production default.

For each SQL database in primary and recovery, require LRS or ZRS only after region capability and approved-location evidence are validated; permit GRS/GZRS only through a later explicit legal/design decision proving the Azure paired secondary is approved and within the signed boundary.
Apply the choice to both short-term and long-term retention, record that changes affect future backups, and require configuration evidence before data admission.
Add Phase 4/5 tests that inspect the rendered ARM property and deployed configuration without claiming deployment in Phase 3.

Add the current Microsoft Learn automated-backups source to the source register and align the Markdown, catalogue, reliability contract, handoff, validation evidence and diagrams where materially affected.

findings.title: APIM private endpoint is not coupled to explicit public gateway disablement
evidence: 3-azure-design/evidence/stratton-source-register.json SRC-AZ-019 says public network access is explicitly disabled after private DNS validation.
3-azure-design/evidence/stratton-network-security-contract.json creates an APIM private endpoint but its policyGuardrails list omits API Management public-network denial.

3-azure-design/evidence/stratton-aff4-handoff.json module 10 outputs only the APIM private endpoint; the compile assertion 'all supported data/AI services disable public network access' does not unambiguously include the API gateway.
Microsoft Learn states that an APIM private endpoint supports private ingress but public network access must be disabled separately, and only after the private endpoint is configured.
findings.risk: The API Management gateway can remain reachable through its public endpoint even while the documented private endpoint works. A caller could bypass the private Application Gateway WAF, enterprise-network registration gate and intended ingress path, increasing attack surface and contradicting the no-public-frontend and fail-closed network boundary.
boundedRemediation: Make API Management publicNetworkAccess=Disabled explicit for dev, test, production-primary and production-recovery after private endpoint approval and private DNS resolution succeed.
Add an API Management-specific compile assertion, Azure Policy or deployment check, PSRule/custom rule and release evidence; a generic data/AI assertion is insufficient.
Require tests proving the public APIM gateway is unreachable and the private Application Gateway-to-APIM path remains functional; prohibit temporary or recovery fallback to the public gateway.

Align the network contract, AFF-4 handoff, catalogue, Markdown and validation receipt. Include App Configuration in the same explicit supported-service public-access review so the private configuration plane is not left to implication.

verdictRationale: The frozen subject has strong and complete logical traceability, coherent identity and assurance separation, bounded AI governance, explicit residual controls and an appropriate Phase 3 boundary. However, two concrete implementation-path defects remain: Azure SQL's default geo-redundant backup storage can silently replicate STR/LTR backups to an unapproved paired region, and an APIM private endpoint does not itself disable the public gateway. Both defects undermine core sovereignty and private-ingress requirements and are MAJOR. An unresolved MAJOR is incompatible with a conforming verdict.
